1. Introduction                                                              Recent research has demonstrated that MLLMs’ visual
                                                                         perception ability remains fundamentally weaker than their
Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) [5, 41, 54,
                                                                         linguistic reasoning, with low-level perceptual failures iden-
56] have achieved impressive progress in scene understand-
                                                                         tified as a primary bottleneck for high-level multimodal rea-
ing [22, 23, 29, 37], visual question answering [18, 19],
                                                                         soning tasks [24, 30, 33, 53]. In mathematical multimodal

3. Method                                                                                 taneously identifies the error type and generates corrective

framework for multimodal reasoning in large language                                      neous reasoning trace ỹi , and ground truth yi , the module
models, featuring a closed-loop Memory Cycle that enables                                 produces both error indicator and corresponding guideline
the agent to continuously learn from its reasoning and per-                               within a single model invocation, formally expressed as:
ception errors—facilitating progressive, lifelong learning.

Figure 2. Overview of the ViLoMem framework. (a) Memory Cycle: A closed-loop learning mechanism where both logical and visual
memories are retrieved and utilized by the solver. Retrieval is conditioned on the textual question and its paired image. The solver then
performs reasoning steps (actions), which are evaluated by the verifier to filter redundant or invalid trajectories. The remaining trajectories
are used to update both memory streams according to their respective types. (b) Memory Generation: An error-attribution framework that
employs an LLM for logical analysis and an MLLM for visual analysis, producing structured memory schemas through similarity-based
merge and create operations. (c) Memory Retrieval: Specialized dual-stream retrieval mechanism. Visual memories undergo a two-stage
process involving image-embedding retrieval followed by question-specific retrieval, since visual information must be conditioned on both
image content and the textual query. Logical memories are retrieved through problem analysis and text-embedding similarity.

To stress-test long-term memory growth, we construct                    domain transfer behavior—task-aligned domains benefit
a progressive memory pool by sequentially accumulat-                    from shared memory, whereas domain-mismatched tasks
ing memories from four math-domain benchmarks: Math-                    exhibit mild interference. Moreover, cross-model trans-
Glance [30], MathVista [24], MathVision [36], and Math-                 fer experiments highlight that our memory can distill er-
Verse [51]. This sequence follows a visual-to-reasoning                 ror patterns and reasoning strategies from stronger models
progression: we first build memory on diagram perceptual                to smaller ones, demonstrating its potential as a lightweight
tasks (MathGlance) and then transition to visual grounded               knowledge-sharing mechanism without explicit fine-tuning.
reasoning tasks. The resulting pool contains ∼3k samples                By enabling progressive error reduction without catas-
and 150k memory tokens. We then evaluate on the unseen                  trophic forgetting, ViLoMem builds a foundation for con-
WeMath [25]. This setup simulates a realistic long-horizon              tinual learning in multimodal reasoning.
